blocks.title: A profile on a language-exchange site
blocks.context: Karim wants to practise his French with a partner.
blocks.fr:
Bonjour à tous !
Je m'appelle Karim, j'ai 34 ans et je suis algérien. J'habite à Laval avec ma femme et mes deux enfants. Je suis infirmier dans un hôpital.
Je parle arabe, anglais et un peu français. J'aime le soccer, la cuisine et les films québécois.
Je cherche un partenaire pour parler français le samedi matin, dans un café ou en ligne. Vous parlez français et vous voulez apprendre l'arabe ? Écrivez-moi !
À bientôt,
Karim
blocks.en: Hello everyone! My name is Karim, I'm 34 and I'm Algerian. I live in Laval with my wife and my two children. I'm a nurse in a hospital. I speak Arabic, English and a little French. I like soccer, cooking and Québec films. I'm looking for a partner to speak French with on Saturday mornings, in a café or online. You speak French and you want to learn Arabic? Write to me! See you soon, Karim

blocks.prompt: What can Karim offer his partner?
blocks.explain: [[Vous voulez apprendre l'arabe ? Écrivez-moi !]] An exchange means each person helps the other.

blocks.title: What the form asks, and how to answer
head: On the form
Example answer
English
blocks.note: For **Profession**, write the job alone, with no article: [[ingénieur]], not *un ingénieur*. Same in a sentence: [[Je suis ingénieur.]]

blocks.title: Capital letters: fewer than in English
blocks.body:
French uses **capitals** for the names of people, cities, countries and streets: [[Karim]], [[Laval]], [[le Canada]], [[rue Sainte-Catherine]].

French uses **no capitals** for:
- days and months: [[lundi]], [[mars]]
- languages: [[Je parle anglais et français.]]
- nationality adjectives: [[Je suis algérien.]] (but *people* as nouns take a capital: [[les Québécois]])
- the words *rue*, *avenue*, *boulevard* in an address: [[avenue Van Horne]]

blocks.title: Accents are part of the spelling
blocks.body:
An accent is not decoration: it can change the meaning.

- [[a]] (has) vs [[à]] (to, at, in): [[Elle a 30 ans et elle habite à Québec.]]
- [[ou]] (or) vs [[où]] (where): [[Tu habites où ?]]
- [[Marie]] (a first name) vs [[marié]] (married)

Accents are also correct on capitals, and recommended both in France and in Québec: [[ÉCOLE]], [[Émilie]], [[À VENDRE]].

blocks.title: Spaces before punctuation: France and Canada
blocks.body:
In **France**, a space goes **before** [[: ; ? !]] (a non-breaking space, so the mark never starts a new line): [[Tu es libre ? Super !]]. This app uses that style.

In **Québec**, the Office québécois de la langue française (OQLF) recommends a space before the **colon**: [[Nom : Patel]]. Before [[; ? !]], it allows **no space** or only a very thin one, so you often see [[Tu es libre? Super!]].

Both styles are correct. In an exam or a formal text, choose **one** and use it everywhere. In every style: no space before a comma or a period, a **comma** in prices ([[5,50 $]]), and no space inside an email address.

blocks.title: Forms in Canada
blocks.body:
- **Dates:** official Canadian forms often use **year-month-day**: [[1991-03-12]]. A French form from France uses day/month/year: [[12/03/1991]]. Check the boxes (AAAA-MM-JJ = YYYY-MM-DD).
- **Addresses:** in French, the number comes first, then a comma: [[4520, avenue Van Horne]]. In a written address, the province often goes in brackets: [[Montréal (Québec)]] (on an envelope, Canada Post uses the abbreviation QC).
- **Postal codes:** letter, number, letter, space, number, letter, number: [[H3S 1R9]].
- **Courriel** is the Québec word for email; [[cellulaire]] (or [[cell]]) is a cell phone.
- **Never** write your social insurance number ([[NAS]]) on a simple community form: only employers and the government need it.

- [[Je suis 34 ans]] → [[J'ai 34 ans]] (age uses **avoir**)
- [[Je suis un infirmier]] → [[Je suis infirmier]] (no article for jobs)
- [[Je parle Anglais]] → [[Je parle anglais]] (no capital for languages)
- A woman writes [[mariée]], [[divorcée]], [[étudiante]]; [[célibataire]] is the same for everyone.
- On a form, [[Nom]] is **not** your full name: just the family name.

blocks.title: Useful profile sentences
blocks.body: Mix and match these chunks to build a profile.

blocks.title: Listen and repeat
blocks.note: At a front desk, people often ask for your details out loud.

lines.fr: Mon nom, c'est Patel : P, A, T, E, L.
lines.en: My last name is Patel: P, A, T, E, L.
lines.tip: Spell slowly, one letter at a time.

lines.fr: Ma date de naissance, c'est le vingt-trois juillet mille neuf cent quatre-vingt-dix.
lines.en: My date of birth is July 23, 1990.
lines.tip: Years: mille neuf cent… (1900s) or deux mille… (2000s).

lines.fr: J'habite au cent vingt-cinq, rue Principale.

blocks.fr: Ma date de naissance, c'est le treize juin mille neuf cent quatre-vingt-huit.
blocks.en: My date of birth is June 13, 1988.
blocks.prompt: What is the date of birth?

blocks.fr: Je suis mariée et je suis professeure.
blocks.en: I'm married and I'm a teacher. (woman)

blocks.prompt: Raj Patel fills in a form. What does he write after “Nom :”?
blocks.explain: [[Nom]] = family name only, often in capitals. [[Raj]] goes after [[Prénom]].
Age uses **avoir** ([[j'ai 29 ans]]); marital status uses **être** ([[je suis célibataire]]).

options: J'habite à Moncton. Je parle anglais et français.
J'habite à moncton. Je parle Anglais et Français.
j'habite à Moncton. je parle anglais et français.
J'habite a Moncton. Je parle anglais et français.
optionFeedback: Cities take a capital; languages don't.
A sentence always starts with a capital letter.
à (in, to) needs its accent; a means has.

blocks.text: Elle ___ deux enfants et elle habite ___ Gatineau.
blocks.en: She has two children and she lives in Gatineau.
blocks.explain: [[a]] without an accent is the verb avoir (has). [[à]] with an accent means in / to.

blocks.prompt: I'm married (woman speaking) and I have two children.
accept: Je suis mariée et j'ai deux enfants.
Je suis mariée, et j'ai deux enfants.
Je suis mariée et j'ai 2 enfants.
blocks.explain: [[mariée]] takes -e for a woman; children uses **avoir**: [[j'ai deux enfants]].

blocks.prompt: I'm a nurse (man speaking) and I live in Laval.
accept: Je suis infirmier et j'habite à Laval.
Je suis infirmier, et j'habite à Laval.
blocks.explain: Jobs take no article after [[je suis]]: [[Je suis infirmier]]. Cities take [[à]].

blocks.prompt: In Québec style (OQLF), which punctuation mark takes a full space before it?
blocks.explain: Québec style: [[Nom : Patel]], but usually [[Tu viens?]] with no space (or only a thin one) before ? ! and ;. France style puts a space before all four: [[: ; ? !]]
optionFeedback: In Québec, ? takes no space or only a thin one. A full space before ? is the France style.
No space before a comma, in any style.

blocks.prompt: I'm looking for a partner to speak French with.
accept: Je cherche un partenaire pour parler français
blocks.explain: [[chercher]] = to look for, with no extra word for *for*: [[je cherche un partenaire]].

blocks.fr: Je suis célibataire et je n'ai pas d'enfants.
accept: Je suis célibataire et je n'ai pas d'enfant.

blocks.prompt: Part 1: fill in the form lines for yourself (Nom, Prénom, Ville, Courriel, Situation de famille, Profession, Langues). You can invent an address and email. Part 2: write a short profile for a language-exchange site or a community centre: who you are, where you live, your family, your work or studies, your languages, what you like, and what you are looking for.
blocks.promptFr: Remplissez le formulaire, puis écrivez votre profil.
checklist: One sentence with Je cherche… or Je voudrais…

summary:
- Fill in a form: [[nom, prénom, date de naissance, adresse, code postal, courriel, situation de famille, profession]]
- Write a short profile with age (avoir), job without an article, languages and likes
- Use capitals and accents the French way, and know the France and Québec spacing styles

meta.notes: Rewrote the France/Québec spacing note to match OQLF guidance (space before the colon; none or a thin space before ; ! ?) and rebuilt quiz r8 around it. Removed informal or France-only answers from the accept lists of the 'Écrivez-moi' and 'courriel' cards. Fixed the marie/marié example and added a few accepted variants.
